view: This week's drop is idiosyncratic to NVDA, not sector-wide: NVDA -15.45% while SOX +7.99%, SMH +4.83%, AMD +30.2%, AVGO +17.46%, TSM +7.53% and SPX -0.45%. It sits on top of a year-long relative downtrend vs SOX (-43.9% over 52w), so leadership inside AI semis has rotated to AMD/AVGO. Relative strength gives no bottom signal yet; I widen the tails versus base rates and lean slightly less bullish than base on the quarters, with the 2026-11-17 print as the swing factor.

probabilities.defs: 2w ±5%, quarters ±10%, vs price_at_call 165.785. next_2_weeks: up > 174.07, down < 157.50 at the 2026-11-26 close. this_quarter: to the 2026-12-31 close; next_quarter: to the 2027-03-31 close; up > 182.36, down < 149.21. up + range + down = 100.

evidence.point: Outside view (n=258): up 33 / range 45 / down 22. My 2w call is 34/33/33: range cut 12 pts and down raised 11 pts, because realized volatility is far above normal (atr_daily_pct 5.9, volume_spike_ratio_mon 3.6) and earnings fall inside the window, so a ±5% band is easy to break either way.
Base 39/43/18 (n=253). I move to 35/34/31: down +13 because the relative trend is negative on every horizon and the shock is company-specific, which a sector rally does not lift.
Base 50/31/19 (n=247). I move to 44/27/29: still up-skewed (NVDA's long-run drift) but less so, given 52w underperformance vs both SOX and SPX.
1W: NVDA -15.45% vs SOX +7.99%, SMH +4.83%, AMD +30.2%, AVGO +17.46%, TSM +7.53%, SPX -0.45%, NDX +1.6%. Every peer and index is up or flat; the move is NVDA-specific.
NVDA lagged SOX by 23.4 points this week, consistent with an idiosyncratic (key-person / governance) shock rather than a sector de-rating.
NVDA/SOX ratio down 13.7% over 13w (18.1331 -> 15.6556) and 43.9% over 52w (from 27.9202). The relative downtrend predates this week; this week accelerated it.
NVDA vs SPX: -25.0% over 13w and -23.2% over 52w. YTD NVDA -12.67% vs SOX +45.29%, SMH +36.99%, AMD +169.15%, SPX +11.14%: NVDA has been a source of funds for AI-semis rotation all year.

Beta vs SOX 0.44 and correlation 0.52 (59w): NVDA now trades only loosely with the semis index, so a strong SOX is weak support for NVDA in the short run. Beta vs SPX 1.42 (59w) vs 1.75 (tv_relative, 1y): market sensitivity is high, so an index pullback would hit NVDA harder.

Breadth is not the problem: RSP 1m +4.03% vs SPY 1m -2.12%, s5th_pct_above_200d 63.81, VIX 17.62. The market is broadening away from mega-cap leaders, which fits continued NVDA relative weakness rather than a risk-off washout.

After 2w drops of 15% or more, NVDA was up or flat in all n=4 2w cases and up in all 4 13w cases (median 13w +32.1%). Tiny, overlapping sample, and this week's move (week_change_pct -11.2 from the 186.64 weekly close) may not even qualify; treated as weak evidence only.

What relative strength does after a key-person shock: I have no NVDA or peer event study in the slice. From judgment only: when the market treats a single-name governance shock as idiosyncratic while the sector rallies, the relative gap tends to close partly if the shock resolves without a thesis break, and keeps widening if it escalates (TB2). That is a binary, not a trend signal, and the earnings call will probably decide which branch.

key_levels.why: Week low so far; a daily close below it extends the idiosyncratic breakdown while peers hold up.
Week open; reclaiming it would be the first sign the NVDA-specific selling is fading.
Lower edge of the unfilled gap (179.92-185.22); filling it would close most of this week's relative gap to SOX.
Previous weekly close, the level before the shock week.
NVDA/SOX ratio now. A ratio that keeps falling while SOX rises means continued rotation out of NVDA; a ratio back toward the 13w-ago 18.1331 would mean the shock has been priced out.

what_would_change_my_mind: More bullish: NVDA outperforms SOX for the week after earnings (week ending 2026-11-20) and closes above the 173.065 week open, showing the shock is being priced out.
More bullish: a daily close back inside the 179.92-185.22 gap by 2026-11-26.
More bearish: SOX turns down while NVDA still underperforms it (beta to the sector reasserting on the downside), or NVDA closes below 157.50 before 2026-11-26.
More bearish: any of TB1-TB4 fires (especially TB2, CEO departure under legal pressure); that would turn an idiosyncratic shock into a thesis break.
Neutral-to-bullish: AMD/AVGO give back a large part of this week's gains while NVDA holds above 165.89, which would show the rotation was a crowded short-term trade.
notes_for_chair: Before vs after the print (2026-11-17 after close): before, relative strength says idiosyncratic weakness inside a strong sector, and that argues against reading 'cheap vs peers' as a buy signal. After, one week of NVDA vs SOX/SMH relative performance is the cleanest read on whether the market accepts guidance despite the key-person issue. I would update by up to 10 pts on that alone.

Data inconsistency: tv_relative nvda_perf_w is -15.45% but structure.week_change_pct is -11.2% (vs the 186.64 weekly close). These are probably different windows (rolling 5 days vs calendar week). Please reconcile before anyone cites a weekly figure.
Beta vs SPX differs by source: 1.42 (59w, relative) vs 1.75 (1y, tv_relative). The direction is the same (high market sensitivity).

Cross-domain: the cause of the shock (governance / key-person) belongs to the news/fundamentals member; I only observe that the market priced it as NVDA-specific. Options positioning is not in my slice, so I cannot say whether the relative gap is driven by hedging flows.

Rotation risk: SOX YTD +45.29% and AMD YTD +169.15% are extended. If semis correct, NVDA's low sector correlation (0.52) could cushion it, but its 1.42-1.75 SPX beta could cut the other way. That is unresolved.
Overlap: I have not used momentum oscillators (RSI etc.); the conditional RSI base rate belongs to the technical member's evidence group.
